While MECP2 Duplication Syndrome is caused by increased gene dosage of MECP2, leading to disruption of neuronal development and neurological dysfunction, dysregulation of the PI3K-Akt pathway, potentially through interaction with AKT1 or other downstream effectors, can contribute to the phenotypic spectrum.

**How to falsify it:** Absence of PIK3CA gain-of-function mutations in a significant proportion of ovarian cancer cases, or demonstration that MECP2 duplication does not impact PI3K-Akt pathway signaling in any capacity. _(variant: rs17849022)_

**Why it matters:** Targeting the PI3K-Akt pathway is a validated therapeutic strategy for ovarian cancer. Investigating the role of this pathway in MECP2 Duplication Syndrome could reveal novel therapeutic avenues for neurological manifestations.
